Yes. The DR2 catalogue (`legaCdr2.fits.gz`, columns per `data/raw/legac_dr2/VizieR_ReadMe.txt`, Straatman et al. 2018, ApJS 239, 27) has `SIGMA_STARS_PRIME_err` next to `SIGMA_STARS_PRIME`, and likewise `SIGMA_GAS_PRIME_err` for the gas dispersion, all in km/s.

Two things to keep in mind: the "PRIME" values are spatially integrated, so they fold in rotation as well as true dispersion, and a handful of rows have nonsense errors (the ReadMe range goes up to 4.7e12 km/s). In the file, 1841 of 1988 spectra have a stellar sigma with a finite error, 5 of those errors exceed 1000 km/s, and the typical error is about 15 km/s, roughly 10% of sigma.
